Subject: Clarify: when prefix-cache hits are billed?

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the recent demo — the latency improvements look promising. Before we lock the SOW, procurement has pushed back on one line item: how "prefix/prompt cache hits" are metered on the hosted API. Our legal and finance teams are worried about surprising charges when we run large batched inference across many similar prompts.

Can you please provide:
- A short, concrete matrix with 3–4 example request patterns (same prompt repeated, prompt with variable slot values, session continuation, partial-match reuse) and whether the request would be billed as full tokens, partial tokens, or not charged at all.
- Any contractual language you recommend for the SOW about reconciliation/credits if we see disputed billing from cache behavior.
- Whether Redwood will cap unexpected cache-hit charges during an initial pilot/test window.

I attached a csv with two of our real prompt families (lumen_prefix_examples.csv) to make the scenarios concrete.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: when prefix-cache hits are billed?

Jordan — thanks for sending the examples, this is a great starting point. Short answers up front:

- Metering principle: our hosted API invoices on net-new model work. When tokens are served from Redwood's prefix (or KV) cache and no model compute is required to re-derive them, those tokens are not billed as new input tokens.
- Partial/transform cases: if the request reuses a cached prefix but adds or changes user content such that the model must recompute later tokens, the system attributes billing to the net-new portion. That can appear as a "partial hit" in invoices.
- Pilot credits: we can offer a temporary credit bucket for the pilot period and do a monthly reconciliation if listings of disputed hits are provided.

I attached a short two-page matrix (redwood_prefix_billing_matrix.pdf) with the four scenario rows you asked for — same prompt repeat, templated slot substitution, continuing session (KV cache reuse), and prompt with structural edits. The matrix shows the likely billed outcome, the key technical reason, and a suggested SOW clause.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will loop in Ben (billing) and Marissa (legal/enterprise ops) to draft the provisional SOW language and the pilot credit cap.
2) If you can flag 4–6 representative requests from your csv that you care about most, we’ll run a short test pass against our staging endpoint to produce an invoice sample.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk the matrix.

—Naomi

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 13:30:00 -0700

Looping you both in — I drafted a short reconciliation proposal and suggested contract snippet. Key points:

- Pilot credit: Redwood will establish a $10k pilot credit pool for the first 90 days tied to the LUM-ENT-2027-08 deal. Any disputed cache-related charges submitted with request fingerprints and timestamps will be evaluated and potentially refunded from that pool.
- Metering breakdown: We should provide three billing examples converted to token-level numbers for their CSV rows. This avoids ambiguity on invoices.
- Language suggestion for SOW (for review/legal): "Redwood shall provide a pilot credit applied against invoiced usage for the first 90 days following production go-live. If Customer identifies suspected misattribution of cached tokens, Customer will submit request identifiers and Redwood will reconcile the usage report and, if validated, apply credit adjustments within the next invoice cycle."

Attachment: lumen_prefix_examples.csv contains the rows I used to build the token examples. Naomi — can you please confirm that $10k pilot cap and that our ops team can do the sample invoice generation? Marissa — if you concur, I’ll shepherd this into the SOW as an addendum.

—Ben
